problem:
Find the solution to the initial value problem

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)={x}_{1}(t)-{x}_{2}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=-2{x}_{1}(t)+2{x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned},\,x(1)=[\begin{aligned}-2{e}^{4} \\ {e}^{4}\end{aligned}].
$$

*Hint: The eigenvalues of the system's matrix are ${\lambda }_{1}=3$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=0.$*

activity_context.topic_title: Solving Homogeneous Systems of ODEs With Distinct Eigenvalues and Initial Conditions

feedback.problem:
Find the solution to the initial value problem

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=5{x}_{1}(t)-3{x}_{2}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=2{x}_{2}(t),\end{aligned}\,x(0)=[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we write down the matrix differential equation ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)$ for the given system:

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}5 & -3 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}]
$$

We need to find the eigenvalues and the eigenvectors of the matrix $A.$

First, we write down the matrix differential equation ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)$ for the given system:

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}5 & -3 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}]
$$

We need to find the eigenvalues and the eigenvectors of the matrix $A.$

- Since $A$ is upper-triangular, the eigenvalues are 

$$
{\lambda }_{1}=5\,\text{and}\,{\lambda }_{2}=2.
$$

- Let's go through the process of finding the eigenvectors.

- For ${\lambda }_{1}=5,$ we get 

$$
A-{\lambda }_{1}I=[\begin{aligned}0 & -3 \\ 0 & -3\end{aligned}]∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

So, we get an eigenvector 
${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$

- For ${\lambda }_{2}=2,$ we get 

$$
A-{\lambda }_{2}I=[\begin{aligned}3 & -3 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

So, we get an eigenvector 
${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

Now, we write down the general solution to the given linear system of differential equations:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & ={c}_{1}{v}_{1}{e}^{{\lambda }_{1}t}+{c}_{2}{v}_{2}{e}^{{\lambda }_{2}t} \\  & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{5t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{2t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find the values of ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}.$ Substituting $t=0$ into the general solution, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(0) & =[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\ {c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{0}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{0} & =[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{c}_{1}+{c}_{2} \\ {c}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}{c}_{1}+{c}_{2}=-5 \\ {c}_{2}=3.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get ${c}_{2}=3.$ Substituting into the first equation, we obtain ${c}_{1}=-8.$ 

Finally, we write down the solution to the initial value problem:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =-8[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{5t}+3[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{2t}\end{aligned}
$$
